The contract (problem.txt) explicitly requires that every K-column be dequantized with the scale/zero of the group it belongs to "for any K -- including a K that is not an exact multiple of group_size", with scales/zeros supplied as ceil(K/group_size) rows. The host wrapper (kernel.py:69-73) instead computes num_groups = K // group_size (floor) and clamps g_idx to num_groups-1, so trailing partial-group columns reuse the previous full group's scale/zero row and the final supplied row is never read.

Probe t6 executed the real kernel on GPU against an explicit unpack+dequant reference using group_of(k)=k//group_size. Control case K=64, gs=32 (exact multiple): max_abs = 2.86e-6, rel = 1.9e-7 -- confirming the reference's packing/zero-point (+1) conventions match the kernel, so the reference is valid. Contract-admitted partial cases: K=48, gs=32 (ceil = 2 rows) gave max_abs = 10.90 against ref_absmax = 13.56 (rel 0.803); K=96, gs=64 gave max_abs = 9.75 vs 14.57 (rel 0.669). The wrapper's g_idx for K=48/gs=32 contains unique values [0] while the contract requires [0,1].

This is a required-behaviour violation on inputs the contract explicitly admits, not a precision or convention difference, so the verdict is reject.
